answer: LINE (Large-scale Information Network Embedding) explicitly defines and optimizes objective functions that preserve both first-order proximity (direct connections between vertex pairs, modeled by making the joint distribution of connected nodes similar to the empirical distribution) and second-order proximity (neighborhood similarity, where nodes sharing many neighbors have similar embeddings), using edge-sampling stochastic gradient descent over an explicit loss on the network structure. DeepWalk, by contrast, does not define an explicit graph-structure objective; it treats truncated random walks over the graph as sentences and applies the Skip-gram language-model approach (with hierarchical softmax) to maximize the likelihood of observing a vertex's neighborhood context within a window in those walks. DeepWalk describes its approach as learning latent social representations of vertices by modeling a stream of short random walks as a language, i.e., an unsupervised, online representation learning method that encodes social relations in a continuous vector space that is easy to use in statistical models.
